transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump is in the Philippines on his Asia trip.
He'll later meet with China and Russia's presidents, but NPR's Deepa Shivaram reports Trump has
already concluded his first talks with leaders of the nations known as the Quad.
So in addition to the U.S., that includes India, Australia, and Japan, these are major
democratic nations, and this group was formed to balance power in the Pacific region against
China.
So timing-wise, it's pretty significant that Trump is able to meet with them before he
meets with Xi in China.
And PR's Deepa Shivaram reporting.
President Trump has already made his first announcement regarding the Quad nations.
Today we're also announcing that the Quad will conduct an exercise featuring our maritime
patrol aircraft as we continue to protect peace through strength.
Next, President Trump is expected to participate in a trade deal signing.
The Trump administration is pressing Congress for tens of billions of dollars in additional
funding to fast-track upgrades to the nation's air traffic control systems.
This follows Friday's nationwide ground stop of flights that stranded travelers.
And PR's Sam Greenglass has more.
This fall, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy had been urging lawmakers to allocate 30 billion
more dollars for an ongoing project to modernize the aging infrastructure.
That figure ballooned to 50 billion after the Friday ground stop, as the Trump administration
partially blamed congressional inaction for the crisis.
But Democrats say Congress has already given the administration more than 14 billion dollars
for this, and some 9 billion has not been spent.
Meanwhile, a September report from the Government Accountability Office warned the speed the
modernization was moving under the Trump administration could result in outages.
Sam Greenglass, NPR News, Washington.
A group of House Democrats wants an investigation into billions of dollars in contracts for
border barriers in the West Texas region of Big Bend.
For Marfa Public Radio, Mary Cantrell reports they're asking the Homeland Security Department's
Inspector General for information.
In a letter, the House Democrats expressed concern about known ties between the Trump
administration and two construction firms awarded lucrative Big Bend border wall projects.
The DHS secretary's waiving of federal contracting laws in the name of a border emergency is
also worth scrutinizing, they say, given the area's low levels of migrant crossings.
Congresswoman-elect Katie Padilla Stout will soon represent the region and says she supports
a probe.
I think that the people deserve transparency, I think one of the ways we can get that in
accountability is through seeing the contract and seeing the investigation behind that.
They're asking for a response from the inspector general by the end of the week.
For NPR News, I'm Mary Cantrell in Marfa.
You're listening to NPR.
The Trump administration has issued a new rule closing a loophole on how certain foreign
countries can buy and use U.S. computer chips.
The rule targets companies that then rent out these computer chips' power to companies
with headquarters in other countries, such as China.
The new rule comes after the head of computer chip maker Invidia stepped down after admitting
an affair.
Reports indicate Jensen Huang was involved with a woman recruited to spy for China.
One of Mexico's most notorious drug lords has died, and he'd been in prison for nearly
40 years.
He was widely known as El Jefe de Jefe, the boss of bosses.
That's because in the '70s and '80s Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo helped wrangle disparate
and warring drug cartels into one centrally-run organization that he called the Federation.
That eventually led to Mexican cartels becoming some of the biggest drug-running organizations
in the world.
Gallardo was convicted of murdering DEA agent Kiki Camarena and has been in jail since 1989.
The U.S. sought his extradition, but he was widely believed to hold secrets about some
of the most powerful figures in Mexico.
And now he has died without ever revealing the secrets.
According to Jalisco state authorities, Gallardo succumbed to organ failure.
He was 80 years old.
A to Peralta and PR News, Mexico City.
AAA says 81.5 million Americans will travel over Thanksgiving.
That's a slight dip from last year when 81.6 million traveled.
The group cites higher travel costs.
It's NPR.

topics.text: President Trump meets Quad leaders in the Philippines during his Asia trip, ahead of China talks
Trump administration pushes Congress for $50 billion to modernize air traffic control after nationwide ground stop
House Democrats request inspector general probe of Big Bend border wall contracts in West Texas
Trump administration issues rule closing loophole on foreign rental of U.S. computer chips, targeting China
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down after admitting an affair with a woman recruited to spy for China
Mexican drug lord Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, known as El Jefe de Jefes, dies in prison at 80
